AfterDamageReceived.issue: Closed 2026-07-29 (round 7): AfterDamageReceived only LATCHES now. CurlUpPower.cs:34-54 records `cardSource` and returns; CurlUpPower.cs:56-70 (AfterCardPlayed) is what gains the block, once the whole card play has resolved, and removes the power. Granting inside the damage hook meant the SECOND and later hits of a multi-hit attack were absorbed by block the game had not handed out yet. powers.py's CurlUpPower carries all three latch guards -- the owner, `props.IsPoweredAttack()`, a non-null cardSource -- plus the no-re-latch clause, and grants UNPOWERED block from `on_card_played`. EXECUTED: a Twin Strike into a Curl Up 8 removes 10 HP (5 + 5, neither hit blocked) and leaves 8 block, where the sim used to absorb the second hit; a bare `DamageCmd.deal` with no card latches nothing at all. TWO LEGACY TESTS MOVED (non-negotiable 5): test_powers.py's whole `TestCurlUp` class drove `DamageCmd.deal` directly and is rewritten around a card PLAY (with the multi-hit case and the null-cardSource guard added), and test_hive.py's `test_curl_up_blocks_on_first_hit` is now `test_curl_up_blocks_after_the_card_play_that_hit_it`. NOT CLOSED: the two guards this entry defers to their own entries are unchanged.  The text it replaced read: LIVE. C# only LATCHES the triggering card here and grants nothing; the sim grants the block and expires the power on the spot. CurlUpPower.cs:34-54 records cardSource in internal Data and returns; CurlUpPower.cs:56-70 (AfterCardPlayed) is what actually gains the block, once the whole card play has resolved. powers.py:309-312 calls BlockCmd.apply and _expire() inside the damage hook, so the SECOND and later hits of a multi-hit attack are absorbed by block the game would not have granted yet. The sim's own docstring (powers.py:307-308) states the weaker half of this correctly -- the triggering hit does take full damage -- and then stops one hit short. Reachable from the ported Louse Progenitor (monsters/hive/louse_progenitor.py:34) plus any multi-hit Attack card. Two guards are also missing; see their own entries. Third-file citations, not hashed here.

guards.rationale: STALE 2026-07-29 (round 11): this entry described the PRE-round-7 sim. Today's powers.py CurlUpPower.on_damage_received reads `if target is not self.owner or card is None: return` then `if not is_powered_attack(props): return` (guard order differs from C#'s but AND-composed guards are order-independent) -- matching CurlUpPower.cs:40-43. `is_powered_attack` (valueprops.py:47-49, `ValueProp.MOVE in props and ValueProp.UNPOWERED not in props`) is IsPoweredAttack's own body (ValuePropExtensions.cs:5-12: `props.HasFlag(Move) && !props.HasFlag(Unpowered)`). EXECUTED (probe: .superpowers/sdd/unlabelled/probes/power-1-curlup-probe.py, case g1): a Curl-Up-8 enemy hit by an unpowered card attack (MOVE|UNPOWERED, dealer+card both present) does not latch -- printed `False`. The Juggernaut example this entry originally cited (cards/juggernaut.py -> powers.py JuggernautPower.on_block_gained) turns out to pass no `card` at all (verified: `DamageCmd.deal(..., dealer=self.owner, props=DamageProps.NON_CARD_UNPOWERED)`, no `card=`), so it was never actually a witness for THIS guard specifically -- it is caught by the cardSource==null guard below regardless of props. That does not change the verdict: the props gate itself is present and correct.

STALE 2026-07-29 (round 11): also describes the pre-round-7 sim. Today's guard is `if target is not self.owner or card is None: return` (powers.py, CurlUpPower.on_damage_received) -- a card is required, matching CurlUpPower.cs:44-47. EXECUTED: test/test_powers.py::TestCurlUp::test_a_bare_damage_instance_grants_nothing drives `DamageCmd.deal(cs.hooks, cs.enemy, 1, dealer=cs.player)` with no card and asserts `cs.enemy.block == 0` and the power survives unlatched -- passes today. Also confirmed directly (probe: power-1-curlup-probe.py, case g2, Juggernaut's own card-less shape) -- printed `False` (does not latch).

STALE 2026-07-29 (round 11): also describes the pre-round-7 sim, which granted block immediately and so had no latch to keep. Today's on_damage_received keeps `self._played_card` and returns early when a second, different card deals damage while the first is still pending: `if self._played_card is not None and card is not self._played_card: return` -- the same one-card latch as CurlUpPower.cs:48-52's `if (playedCard != null && cardSource != playedCard) return`. EXECUTED (probe: power-1-curlup-probe.py latch sequence, run inline): card A hits first and latches (`_played_card is card_a` -> True); a different card B then hits while A is still pending and does NOT overwrite the latch (`_played_card is card_a` still True); B finishing its play grants nothing (`block == 0`, power still present); A finishing its play grants the block (`block == 8`) and removes the power. All five assertions matched the C# latch semantics.

STALE 2026-07-29 (round 11): also describes the pre-round-7 sim, whose block grant lived in on_damage_received with no props. Today's on_card_played passes it explicitly: `BlockCmd.apply(self.hooks, self.owner, self.amount, props=ValueProp.UNPOWERED)` -- matching CurlUpPower.cs:63's ValueProp.Unpowered. EXECUTED (probe: power-1-curlup-probe.py, case g4): an enemy with Curl Up 8 AND Frail 1 (which multiplies MOVE-and-not-UNPOWERED block by 0.75, cmds.py BlockCmd modifier gate) still ends the card play at block 8, not 6 -- Frail did not touch it, confirming the block is correctly typed UNPOWERED and the modifier families are skipped.

Same mechanism note as power/shriek's: Curl Up overrides no AfterRemoved, so the observable is identical, but the sim's _expire (powers.py:86-92) bypasses RemoveInternal/AfterRemoved. WHEN the removal happens is the separate gap recorded above.
